answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond that is locked for a fixed period, then slash it if the identity is caught double-claiming rewards or violating challenge rules. A verifier can issue unpredictable tasks and compare signed, time-stamped responses across accounts; matching copied answers trigger review rather than automatic proof of fraud. The willow, knoll, and juniper accounts may all join, but each needs its own capital at risk, so multiplying identities ties up funds and exposes more stake to loss.
